_: WHAT THE MAP'S STATE ENCODING MUST BE ABLE TO SHOW, and against what.
ADR-0047 D6: no state rides a 1px border, and the floor is 3:1 - WCAG
1.4.11, which is the floor for a boundary that IDENTIFIES state rather than
one that decorates. Three states went under it without anybody choosing it,
because color-mix() toward --line quietly eats contrast. This file is what
refuses the next time.
It is DATA, not code, for one reason: the channel that carries a state was
about to move, and in 20e.1 it did. It was the node's 1px border; it is the
4px edge drawn by ::before now, and moving the probe was an edit HERE - the
six probes below and the chain above - with no change to
scripts/check-contrast.mjs at all.
The edge is a background-COLOUR and never a gradient. A dashed edge drawn
with repeating-linear-gradient resolves `background-color` to transparent,
so the gate could not read the one state it was measuring: `working` keeps
its dashed 1px outline as the second visual cue and its 4px edge solid.
The six states are the six ADR-0047 measured. A seventh state on the map
means a seventh line here - a state the contract does not name is not
checked, and the gate says so out loud rather than passing quietly.
PHASE 27: `chain` BECAME `chains`, AND THERE ARE THREE OF THEM. ADR-0058
found that the page had grown a second ancestry - the estate contour draws
the same states under `.contour > .estate-env > .set.estate-set` - while
this contract probed only the map's. No ancestor in either paints a
background, so the colours SHOULD be identical, and `should` is what an
instrument aimed at the wrong scope is made of.
The THIRD was not in that finding. It was found by measuring the BUILT
page instead of reading the template: the assertions contour hangs its
suite nodes straight off `div.suites`, with no `.set` in between. It also
puts `assertion` on every node, which sets `opacity: 1`, and this gate
composites by opacity - so that chain carries an `adds`. A chain that draws
a node the page never draws would be measuring nothing.
`gone` is the seventh state, added for the reason the paragraph above
predicted. Every CSS rule pairs it with `absent` and it is exempt for the
same reason - but until Phase 27 it was a state the page drew and this
contract did not name, which is the sentence above failing to be acted on.

chains.why: the map. The chain this contract has always carried.
the nouns, drawn as a contour of their own since Phase 24 (ADR-0058).
the suites. The third ancestry, and ADR-0058 named only two - measured on the built page rather than read off the template.

states.what: failed in the run still going
its phase is running - which node is unknown
finished in the run still going
a test suite - observed by its report, not by Terraform
an environment that is destroyed - drawn by the estate contour
exempt: The same exemption as `absent`, and not a second decision: every CSS
rule that names one names the other - the grayscale icon, the 0.45
opacity, the dashed border, the muted state word - and neither sets a
::before colour, so both fall to the base edge, var(--line).
It is here because Phase 27 asked what the estate contour actually
draws and found a state the contract had never named. Measured on every
run, exempt from the floor, printed with the rest.
DELIBERATE, and ADR-0047 D6 says so in the decision itself: the absence
of state is carried by the word alone. Drawing 'nothing has happened' as
brightly as 'this failed' is a claim about importance the page should
not make. Written here because a future session reading a table of
numbers without this paragraph will 'fix' it.
Exempt from the FLOOR, not from measurement: it is measured on every run
and printed with the rest, so a change to it is visible.
